**Finding: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

- **Where:** Section 7.0 Materials (p0082–p0086); checked also §12.1 (Base Components licence), §14.17 (Limitation of Licenses), §11.6 (Content responsibility), §14.18 (Data Protection) and the definitions of Content / Customer Components / Materials.
- **Problem:** Deliverables default to **Type II** (IBM/third-party owned), and the Type II licence back is internal-Enterprise-only with **no right to modify or sublicense** — short of even the fallback position. Nothing in the agreement affirmatively confirms we retain ownership of our Content and Customer Components.
- **Not walk-away:** there is no assignment of our IP or data to IBM and no joint ownership; IBM's ownership of Base Components and pre-existing Materials is acceptable.
- **Redline (validated ok:true):** default Materials to Type I (Customer-owned); make the Type II licence perpetual and add modify/derivative-works and sublicensing rights for our business purposes; add a new §7(e) confirming our ownership of Content and Customer Components.
